questions.question: Which reformer is known for his efforts to promote widow remarriage and women’s education in Bengal?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was a prominent Indian social reformer, educator, and writer who played a crucial role in advocating for widow remarriage and women's education during the 19th century.
 
• He was instrumental in the passage of the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856**, which legalized widow remarriage in India.
 
• Vidyasagar worked tirelessly to improve the status of women in society by promoting education for girls and establishing schools for them, including the first women's college in Bengal.
 
• He simplified and modernized the Bengali alphabet and script, making education more accessible to the masses.
 
• Known for his progressive and humanitarian views, Vidyasagar was deeply committed to eradicating social evils such as child marriage and gender inequality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen:**

 
 
• Keshab Chandra Sen was a social reformer and a prominent figure in the Brahmo Samaj movement.
 
• He worked towards the abolition of caste discrimination and untouchability and advocated for women's rights, including education and upliftment.
 
• While he contributed significantly to social reforms, his efforts were not specifically focused on widow remarriage or the promotion of women's education in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Debendranath Tagore:**
 
 
• Debendranath Tagore was an Indian philosopher and religious reformer associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He emphasized spiritual and moral reform in society but did not actively campaign for widow remarriage or women's education.
 
• Debendranath is also known for his contributions to Indian philosophy and his role as the father of Rabindranath Tagore.
 
 
 
• **Swami Vivekananda:**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda was a spiritual leader and philosopher who popularized Indian philosophy and spirituality in the West.
 
• He advocated for social reform, including the upliftment of women, but his primary focus was on spiritual awakening and promoting Vedanta philosophy.
 
• His contributions were significant but did not center around widow remarriage or women's education.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the power of the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes under the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 342**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 342** of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes in consultation with the Governor of the concerned state.
 
• It allows the President to notify specific tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes for the purpose of granting them special rights and privileges.
 
• The Parliament has the authority to include or exclude any tribe from the Scheduled Tribes list after the President's initial notification.
 
• Scheduled Tribes are provided with certain constitutional safeguards to ensure their socio-economic development and to protect their rights.
 
• The provisions under Article 342 aim to address historical injustices and promote the welfare of tribal communities across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 343**

 
 
• It deals with the official language of the Union of India.
 
• Article 343(1) specifies that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
 
• The use of the English language for official purposes was to continue for 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution, but it has been extended through subsequent legislation.
 
 
 
• **Article 336**
 
 
• This article provides special provisions for the Anglo-Indian community concerning services in certain government sectors.
 
• It ensures reservations for Anglo-Indians in the services of the Union and the states for a specified period.
 
• This provision was created to safeguard the employment opportunities of Anglo-Indians during the formative years of independent India.
 
 
 
• **Article 340**
 
 
• It empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• The commission is tasked with suggesting measures to improve the conditions of these classes and recommending steps for their advancement.
 
• This article forms the basis for several welfare schemes and policies aimed at uplifting backward classes in India.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation 'MAN' stand for in computer networking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metropolitan Area Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)** is a type of computer network that spans a geographic area larger than a Local Area Network (LAN) but smaller than a Wide Area Network (WAN).
 
• Typically, a MAN covers a city or a large campus, connecting multiple LANs within the region.
 
• MANs are often used to link buildings, offices, or networks within the same city or metropolitan area to facilitate seamless communication.
 
• They use high-capacity communication links such as fiber optics to provide fast data transfer and connectivity.
 
• MANs play a critical role in connecting different parts of urban areas and enabling efficient data exchange between organizations or public systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mobile Area Network**:

 
 
• Mobile Area Network is not a standard term in computer networking.
 
• It could imply a network that operates on mobile devices or mobile infrastructure, but it is not officially recognized in networking terminologies.
 
 
 
• **Medium Access Network**:
 
 
• This term does not exist in the context of computer networking.
 
• However, "Medium Access Control (MAC)" is a sublayer of the data link layer in the OSI model responsible for regulating how data is transmitted over a shared medium.
 
 
 
• **Main Access Node**:
 
 
• This term is also not a standard abbreviation or concept in computer networking.
 
• Access nodes in a network are devices or points that provide connectivity to the main network, but the term "Main Access Node" is not widely used.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Computer Networking**:

 
 
• Computer networks enable communication and data sharing between devices, such as computers, servers, and other hardware.
 
• Networks are classified into several types based on their geographic scope, such as Local Area Network (LAN), Metropolitan Area Network (MAN), and Wide Area Network (WAN).
 
• Each type of network serves specific purposes, with MAN acting as an intermediary between LAN and WAN in terms of size and functionality.

questions.question: As of June 2025, how many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution recognizes **22 official languages** as of June 2025.
 
• Originally, the Eighth Schedule included **14 languages** when the Constitution of India was adopted in 1950.
 
• Subsequent amendments have added more languages to the list. For instance, the **21st Amendment Act of 1967** included Sindhi, while the **71st Amendment Act of 1992** added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali.
 
• The most recent addition was made through the **92nd Amendment Act of 2003**, which included Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, bringing the total to 22 languages.
 
• The languages listed in the Eighth Schedule are considered to hold special cultural and linguistic significance in India and are eligible for promotion and development under Article 351 of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution primarily deals with the recognition and promotion of languages in India.
 
• The inclusion of a language in this schedule enables its development, preservation, and promotion through various government initiatives.
 
• It also provides a basis for its use in official communication, education, and other spheres of public life.
 
• **Initially**, the Eighth Schedule contained only **14 languages** when the Indian Constitution was adopted in 1950. These languages included Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, and others.
 
• The Eighth Schedule listed 18 languages after the inclusion of Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali through the **71st Amendment Act of 1992**.

questions.question: Which of the following states was NOT formed through the State Reorganisation Act of 1956?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **State Reorganisation Act of 1956** was implemented to redraw the boundaries of Indian states based on linguistic lines.
 
• **Goa** was not formed through the State Reorganisation Act of 1956. It was annexed to India on **19th December 1961** through military action against Portuguese colonial rule.
 
• Goa became a Union Territory in **1961** and was later granted statehood on **30th May 1987**.
 
• The State Reorganisation Act led to the formation or restructuring of several states, but Goa’s inclusion into India was separate and unrelated to this legislative act.
 
• Goa was under Portuguese colonial rule for over 450 years before becoming a part of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan State**

 
 
• Rajasthan was reorganized under the State Reorganisation Act of 1956.
 
• It was formed by merging Ajmer, Abu Road Taluka, Sunel-Tappa (from Madhya Pradesh), and other princely states.
 
• The state is known for its rich cultural heritage and historical significance, including forts, palaces, and desert landscapes.
 
 
 
• **Mysore State**
 
 
• Mysore State was reorganized under the State Reorganisation Act of 1956.
 
• It was later renamed as **Karnataka** in **1973**.
 
• The linguistic reorganization included merging Kannada-speaking regions from other areas into Mysore State.
 
• Karnataka is known for its contributions to Indian culture, architecture, and technology.
 
 
 
• **Bombay State**
 
 
• Bombay State was reorganized in 1956 under the State Reorganisation Act.
 
• It included Marathi-speaking and Gujarati-speaking regions.
 
• Later, Bombay State was bifurcated into **Maharashtra** and **Gujarat** on **1st May 1960**.
 
• The bifurcation was based on linguistic demographics—Marathi-speaking regions formed Maharashtra, while Gujarati-speaking regions formed Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **The State Reorganisation Act of 1956**
 
 
• This act was a major reform in independent India aimed at creating states based on linguistic identities.
 
• The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC), headed by **Fazal Ali**, recommended the changes.
 
• The act resulted in the formation of 14 states and 6 union territories.
 
• It addressed administrative and political challenges caused by linguistic diversity, paving the way for linguistic harmony.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution directs the State for promotion of cottage industries in rural areas?

• **Article 43** of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution directs the State to promote **cottage industries in rural areas** on an individual or cooperative basis.
 
• The objective is to ensure equitable distribution of resources and provide opportunities for employment and economic development in rural areas.
 
• This article is part of Part IV of the Indian Constitution, which encompasses the Directive Principles of State Policy aimed at establishing a welfare state.
 
• Under Article 43, the State endeavors to promote economic and social welfare by fostering self-employment and small-scale industries, especially in rural sectors.
 
• The focus on cottage industries contributes to **rural development, self-reliance, and reducing migration to urban areas** in search of employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 41**

 
 
• This article directs the State to secure the **right to work, education, and public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement within its economic capacity and development limits.
 
• It emphasizes providing social security and welfare for vulnerable sections of the population.
 
 
 
• **Article 36**
 
 
• This article defines the term "State" for the purpose of Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).
 
• The term includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under its control.
 
 
 
• **Article 55**
 
 
• It deals with the **election of the President of India**.
 
• It specifies the manner of voting and the proportional representation system by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• This article does not relate to the promotion of cottage industries or rural development.

questions.question: Which of the following plateaus lies between the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deccan Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a **triangular-shaped landmass** that lies between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats in southern India.
 
• It covers parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala.
 
• The plateau is characterized by **black soil derived from volcanic rocks** and is highly fertile, especially for cotton cultivation.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the **Satpura and Vindhya ranges** in the north and extends southward to the tip of the Indian peninsula.
 
• It is home to several rivers, including the **Krishna, Godavari, and Kaveri**, which originate from the Western Ghats and flow eastward towards the Bay of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhota Nagpur Plateau:**

 
 
• Located in eastern India, this plateau is spread across Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and West Bengal.
 
• It is rich in mineral resources, especially coal, iron ore, mica, and bauxite.
 
• The Damodar River flows through this region, making it a prominent industrial area for steel and power generation.
 
 
 
• **Malwa Plateau:**
 
 
• Situated in western India, covering parts of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
 
• It is bounded by the Aravalli Hills in the northwest and the Vindhya Range in the south.
 
• The plateau is known for black soil and is a major agricultural region for crops like wheat, soybean, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Meghalaya Plateau:**
 
 
• Located in northeastern India, it includes the Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo Hills.
 
• The region is known for heavy rainfall and biodiversity, with Cherrapunji and Mawsynram being among the wettest places on Earth.
 
• It is composed of ancient Archean rocks and is rich in coal and limestone deposits.

questions.question: Which organisation unveiled the strategic report titled 'Designing a Policy for Medium Enterprises' emphasising their role in India’s development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• NITI Aayog is the **policy think tank** of the Government of India, established to provide strategic and technical advice on key developmental issues, including economic growth and social development.
 
• The strategic report titled "**Designing a Policy Framework for Medium Enterprises**" was unveiled by NITI Aayog to **highlight the importance of medium enterprises** in India's economic development.
 
• The report focuses on creating a distinct policy framework for medium enterprises, which often get overshadowed by large corporations and small-scale industries in policymaking.
 
• The aim is to address challenges faced by medium enterprises, such as limited access to credit, inadequate infrastructure, and lack of innovation support, to enhance their contribution to the Indian economy.
 
• This initiative aligns with NITI Aayog's mandate of driving economic growth through evidence-based policy-making and fostering innovation and entrepreneurship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of India responsible for **monetary policy, regulation of financial institutions, and issuance of currency**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in ensuring financial stability and promoting growth by regulating credit flow and inflation.
 
• RBI's focus is on areas like banking supervision, digital payments, and financial inclusion rather than direct policy design for medium enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of MSME**
 
 
• The Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) is responsible for **formulating policies, schemes, and programs for MSMEs**.
 
• It ensures that small and medium enterprises receive adequate support in terms of credit, skill development, and market access.
 
• Though the ministry focuses on MSMEs, the strategic report mentioned in the question was specifically prepared by NITI Aayog.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 246**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 246** of the Indian Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States.
 
• It provides for three lists in the Seventh Schedule: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**, which outline the subjects on which legislation can be enacted.
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, etc., over which only the Parliament has exclusive legislative authority.
 
• The **State List** includes subjects like police, public health, agriculture, etc., where the state legislatures have exclusive powers.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects such as education, marriage, and bankruptcy, where both the Union and State legislatures can legislate.
 
• In case of conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the **Union law prevails**, as per Article 254.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 368:**

 
 
• Article 368 of the Indian Constitution deals with the **procedure for amending the Constitution**.
 
• It provides for two types of amendments: **Simple Majority Amendments** and **Special Majority Amendments**.
 
• Special Majority Amendments require approval by two-thirds of the members present and voting, along with a majority of the total membership of Parliament.
 
• Some amendments also require ratification by half of the State Legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Article 240:**
 
 
• Article 240 empowers the President of India to make **regulations for certain Union Territories**.
 
• These Union Territories include Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu.
 
• The President can legislate on matters concerning these territories, subject to the powers conferred by Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 280:**
 
 
• Article 280 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the **Finance Commission**.
 
• The Finance Commission is responsible for recommending the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States.
 
• It determines the principles for sharing taxes, grants-in-aid to states, and financial relations between different levels of government.

questions.question: What pigment do petunias have that gives them a reddish-purple colour in an acidic environment (low pH)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthocyanins**__.

__
 
• **Anthocyanins** are water-soluble pigments found in plant tissues that are responsible for red, purple, and blue colors in flowers, fruits, and leaves.
 
• In **acidic environments (low pH)**, anthocyanins impart a reddish-purple color, which is why petunias exhibit this coloration under such conditions.
 
• These pigments belong to a class of compounds called flavonoids, which are derived from phenylalanine and are known for their antioxidant properties.
 
• The color of anthocyanins is highly dependent on the pH level of their environment: they appear red in acidic conditions, purple at neutral pH, and blue in alkaline conditions.
 
• Anthocyanins play a critical role in attracting pollinators to flowers like petunias and also in protecting plant tissues from ultraviolet light damage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carotenes**

 
 
• Carotenes are orange, yellow, or red pigments that belong to the carotenoid family and are found in fruits and vegetables such as carrots, pumpkins, and tomatoes.
 
• Unlike anthocyanins, carotenes are fat-soluble pigments and are not pH-sensitive.
 
• They play an essential role in photosynthesis by capturing light energy and are also precursors to Vitamin A in humans.
 
 
 
• **Betalains**
 
 
• Betalains are water-soluble pigments found in plants of the Caryophyllales order, such as beets and bougainvillea.
 
• They are divided into two categories: betacyanins (red-violet) and betaxanthins (yellow-orange).
 
 
 
• **Lycopene**
 
 
• Lycopene is a red carotenoid pigment found in tomatoes, watermelons, and red peppers.
 
• It is known for its antioxidant properties and potential health benefits, such as reducing the risk of certain cancers and heart diseases.

questions.question: Why is the net sown area low in hilly states like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand?

options.text: Because of steep slopes and thin soil layers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because of steep slopes and thin soil layers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hilly states like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand experience steep slopes that make it difficult to carry out large-scale agricultural activities.
 
• The soil in hilly regions is often thin, rocky, and less fertile, which limits the scope of cultivation.
 
• Terrace farming is practiced in some areas, but the total area available for cultivation remains limited due to the topography.
 
• Unfavorable climatic conditions, such as heavy rainfall leading to soil erosion, also impact the availability of arable land.
 
• The forest cover in these regions is extensive, which further reduces the land available for agriculture but is crucial for maintaining ecological balance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Urban expansion refers to the growth of cities and towns into rural areas. While this may reduce agricultural land in urbanized states, it is not a significant factor in hilly regions like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, where urbanization is limited.
 
• These states primarily have rural populations, and the impact of urban expansion on net sown area is negligible compared to geographical and climatic constraints.
 
 
 
• **Because of poor soil fertility**
 
 
• Although soil fertility might be a concern in certain areas, it is not the primary reason for low net sown area in hilly states.
 
• The primary issue is the steep topography and thin soil layers that prevent large-scale agricultural practices, even in areas where the soil may be fertile.
 
 
 
• **Due to frequent floods**
 
 
• Floods are more common in plains and low-lying areas than in hilly regions like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
 
• While these states experience landslides and heavy rainfall, floods are not a major factor affecting the net sown area.

• **Net Sown Area**

 
 
• Net sown area refers to the total area sown with crops in a given agricultural year.
 
• It is a key indicator of agricultural productivity and land usage in a region.
 
• Factors affecting the net sown area include topography, soil quality, climate, irrigation facilities, and population density.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary memory of a computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a type of primary memory that is directly accessible by the CPU.
 
• It temporarily stores data and instructions that the computer is currently using, ensuring faster read/write speeds compared to secondary storage.
 
• RAM is a volatile memory, meaning it loses its contents when the power supply is turned off.
 
• It plays a crucial role in determining the performance of a computer, as it impacts the system's ability to handle multiple tasks efficiently.
 
• Modern computers use DDR (Double Data Rate) RAM, such as DDR4 or DDR5, which provides higher performance and efficiency compared to older types like DDR3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Disk**

 
 
• A hard disk is a type of secondary storage device used to store data permanently.
 
• Unlike RAM, the data stored on a hard disk is non-volatile and remains intact even when the computer is powered off.
 
• It is slower than RAM in terms of data access speed but can store significantly larger amounts of data.
 
• Modern hard disks are being replaced or supplemented by faster storage devices like SSDs (Solid State Drives).
 
 
 
• **CD-ROM**
 
 
• CD-ROM (Compact Disc-Read Only Memory) is an optical storage medium used for reading data that has been written onto it.
 
• It is primarily used for distributing software, music, and other data.
 
• As a read-only memory, data on a CD-ROM cannot be modified once written.
 
• Its storage capacity typically ranges from 650 MB to 700 MB.
 
 
 
• **Floppy Disk**
 
 
• A floppy disk is an outdated magnetic storage medium used for storing small amounts of data.
 
• It was widely used in the 1980s and 1990s but has now been replaced by more modern storage devices such as USB drives and cloud storage.
 
• Floppy disks typically had a storage capacity of 1.44 MB.
 
• Due to their limited storage and slow access speed, floppy disks are now obsolete.

• **Manufacturing Sector:**
 
 
• The manufacturing sector was underdeveloped during colonial rule, and its contribution to the economy was limited.
 
• Small-scale industries dominated manufacturing, with little technological innovation.
 
• Post-independence, the Indian government focused on building a robust manufacturing base, particularly through the establishment of heavy industries and industrial policies.

questions.question: What is the main function of carbohydrates in the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbohydrates are the primary source of energy for the human body, especially for the brain, muscles, and other vital organs.
 
• They are broken down into glucose during digestion, which is then utilized by cells for energy production through cellular respiration.
 
• Each gram of carbohydrate provides 4 kilocalories of energy, making it a highly efficient energy source.
 
• Carbohydrates are stored in the body in the form of glycogen in the liver and muscles, which acts as a reserve energy supply during physical activity or fasting.
 
• Foods rich in carbohydrates include rice, bread, pasta, fruits, vegetables, and legumes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: It is crucial for growth**

 
 
• While carbohydrates play an indirect role in growth by providing energy for cell metabolism, growth primarily depends on proteins, vitamins, and minerals.
 
• Proteins are essential for the synthesis of enzymes, hormones, and structural components, which are necessary for growth and repair.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It regulates hormones**
 
 
• Carbohydrates do not directly regulate hormones; however, they can influence insulin secretion, which is a hormone that regulates blood sugar levels.
 
• Hormonal regulation is primarily carried out by glands in the endocrine system, including hormones like growth hormone, thyroid hormones, and sex hormones.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It insulates the body**
 
 
• Insulation of the body is primarily a function of lipids (fats). Fats form a layer beneath the skin, helping to maintain body temperature by reducing heat loss.
 
• Adipose tissue, which stores fat, plays a crucial role in insulation and energy storage.

questions.question: The Lower Palaeolithic period in India, including the Acheulian phase, spans approximately how many years BP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6,00,000–1,50,000 years BP**__.

__
 
• The Lower Palaeolithic period in India spans approximately **6,00,000 to 1,50,000 years BP (Before Present)**, coinciding with the early Stone Age.
 
• This period is characterized by the use of stone tools, particularly **Acheulian hand-axes and cleavers**, made from quartzite and other available materials.
 
• The Acheulian phase, named after discoveries in Saint-Acheul, France, is known for its **advanced bifacial tools** used for hunting and other purposes.
 
• Prominent Lower Palaeolithic sites in India include **Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu, Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh, and Hunsgi in Karnataka**.
 
• These tools and archaeological evidence suggest that early humans of this time were hunter-gatherers, relying heavily on their tools for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1,65,000–31,000 years BP:**

 
 
• This timeline corresponds to the **Middle Palaeolithic period** in India.
 
• It is marked by the use of **flake tools**, which were smaller and more refined compared to Acheulian tools.
 
• Technological advancements included the use of **Levallois technique** for tool-making.
 
• Sites such as **Nevasa in Maharashtra** and **Paisra in Bihar** represent this era.
 
 
 
• **1,00,000–10,000 years BP:**
 
 
• This period corresponds to the **Upper Palaeolithic period**, characterized by advanced blade and burin tools.
 
• Early evidence of **artistic expression**, such as cave paintings and engravings, is seen during this phase.
 
• Key sites include **Bhimbetka rock shelters**, where prehistoric art depicts the life of early humans.
 
 
 
• **40,000–12,000 years:**
 
 
• This timeline overlaps with the later part of the Upper Palaeolithic period and the transition to the **Mesolithic period**.
 
• Microlithic tools, made from small stone flakes, became predominant during this era.
 
• Humans began to experiment with early forms of **agriculture and domestication of animals**.

questions.question: Who organises Lok Adalats in India?

options.text: National and State Legal Services Authorities

__
 
• Lok Adalats in India are organized by **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)** and **State Legal Services Authorities (SLSAs)** under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• The primary aim of Lok Adalats is to ensure **speedy justice**, reduce the burden on regular courts, and promote amicable dispute resolution.
 
• Cases resolved in Lok Adalats are legally binding, and settlements are treated as **decrees of a civil court.**
 
• They handle cases such as **civil disputes, family disputes, labor disputes, public utility services, and petty criminal cases.**
 
• Lok Adalats emphasize **compromise and mutual agreement** between disputing parties, ensuring cost-effective and accessible justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bar Council of India**

 
 
• It is a statutory body established under the **Advocates Act, 1961**, responsible for regulating the legal profession and legal education in India.
 
• The Bar Council does not organize Lok Adalats but oversees the ethics, conduct, and qualifications of lawyers in India.
 
• It also prescribes standards for legal education and recognizes law universities.
 
 
 
• **Law Commission of India**
 
 
• It is an **advisory body** constituted by the Government of India to suggest legal reforms and recommend changes to existing laws.
 
• The Commission conducts studies and research to improve the justice delivery system but does not directly organize Lok Adalats.
 
• Its recommendations are not binding but have significantly influenced law-making in India.
 
 
 
• **Advocate General of State**
 
 
• The Advocate General is the **highest law officer of the state government**, appointed under Article 165 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The role of the Advocate General is to provide legal advice to the state government and represent it in court cases.
 
• While the Advocate General is involved in legal matters, they are not responsible for organizing Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Lok Adalats are a part of the Indian judicial system and are alternative dispute resolution forums aimed at reducing the burden on the formal courts.
 
• The decisions made in Lok Adalats are **final and cannot be appealed** in any court, ensuring timely resolution of disputes.
 
• These forums are especially beneficial for resolving cases where the parties are willing to settle the matter mutually.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major difference between planted and natural vegetation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human supervision involved**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Planted vegetation refers to crops, plants, or trees grown under human supervision, whereas natural vegetation grows in the wild without any human intervention.
 
• Human supervision in planted vegetation includes activities like sowing seeds, watering plants, providing fertilizers, and controlling pests to ensure their growth and yield.
 
• Natural vegetation develops based on environmental factors such as climate, soil type, and availability of water, without external assistance.
 
• Planted vegetation is often grown for specific purposes such as agriculture, horticulture, or landscaping, while natural vegetation plays a critical role in maintaining ecological balance.
 
• The presence of human supervision in planted vegetation ensures controlled growth and planned outcomes, differentiating it from the spontaneous growth patterns seen in natural vegetation.

• **Presence of fruits:**

 
 
• Fruits are found in both planted and natural vegetation depending on the type of plant species.
 
• The presence of fruits is not a distinguishing factor between planted and natural vegetation.
 
• Planted vegetation might have a higher yield of fruits due to human efforts, but natural vegetation can also produce fruits naturally.
 
 
 
• **Place of origin:**
 
 
• The place of origin refers to where vegetation naturally or artificially grows.
 
• Natural vegetation originates in its native habitat, while planted vegetation can be grown in artificial or controlled environments.
 
• However, place of origin is not the key distinguishing factor between the two types of vegetation.
 
 
 
• **Number of leaves:**
 
 
• The number of leaves is dependent on the type of plant species and its growth pattern.
 
• It is not a relevant parameter to distinguish between planted and natural vegetation.
 
• Both planted and natural vegetation can have varying numbers of leaves based on environmental and genetic factors.

questions.question: What does the term 'net sown area' refer to?

options.text: Total area cultivated with crops during the year
Land left uncultivated for more than five years

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Total area cultivated with crops during the year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **'net sown area'** refers to the total area of land on which crops are cultivated during a year.
 
• It includes land used for the cultivation of all types of crops, whether for food production, commercial purposes, or other agricultural uses.
 
• This measure does not account for multiple cropping (when more than one crop is grown on the same piece of land during a year).
 
• Net sown area is a critical agricultural statistic, as it helps determine the extent of land actively used for farming in a given year.
 
• It is a key indicator in understanding agricultural activity, land use patterns, and food production capacity in any region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total area under irrigation**

 
 
• This refers to the total area of land that is supplied with water through artificial means like canals, wells, and tube wells for agricultural purposes.
 
• It is different from net sown area as irrigation specifically focuses on the availability of water resources rather than the actual cultivation of crops.
 
• Irrigation is critical for ensuring water availability to crops, especially in regions with inadequate or erratic rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Land covered with forests**
 
 
• This refers to the area of land classified as forest by the government, primarily intended for conservation of biodiversity and as a habitat for wildlife.
 
• Forest areas are not counted under agricultural land or net sown area as they are not used for crop cultivation.
 
• Forests play a vital role in maintaining ecological balance and mitigating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Land left uncultivated for more than five years**
 
 
• This refers to land that has not been used for agricultural purposes for an extended period, typically more than five years.
 
• Such land is classified as fallow land or wasteland and is not included in the net sown area.
 
• Land may be left uncultivated due to poor soil fertility, water scarcity, or lack of resources for farming.

questions.question: What is the main aim of globalisation?

• **Globalisation** refers to the integration of economies, cultures, and societies across countries through trade, technology, investment, and communication.
 
• The primary aim of globalisation is to **connect the Indian economy with the global economy**, fostering international cooperation and growth.
 
• It encourages **free flow of goods, services, capital, and technology** between nations, promoting mutual benefits.
 
• Globalisation enhances **economic growth, employment opportunities, and technological advancement** by exposing domestic industries to international competition and innovation.
 
• It also helps in attracting **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, expanding market access, and increasing global trade partnerships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Globalisation promotes foreign trade rather than limiting it.
 
• It eliminates trade barriers like tariffs and import restrictions, enabling countries to exchange goods and services freely.
 
• Limiting foreign trade contradicts the essence of globalisation, which aims to expand trade relations worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Reduce employment**
 
 
• Globalisation often leads to the creation of employment opportunities, especially in sectors like manufacturing, IT, and services, as businesses expand globally.
 
• However, it can sometimes lead to job losses in industries unable to compete internationally, but overall, it is aimed at enhancing economic growth and employment.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Increase local production**
 
 
• Globalisation does not primarily focus on increasing local production; instead, it focuses on integrating global markets.
 
• While it can boost local industries by exposing them to international markets, the concept goes beyond just local production to foster global interconnectedness.

questions.question: The Non-cooperation Movement in 1920 included all the following, EXCEPT:

__
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 as a peaceful resistance against British rule in India.
 
• Violent attacks on officials were explicitly discouraged during the movement, as it was rooted in the principle of non-violence (Ahimsa).
 
• Gandhi believed in achieving independence through peaceful and non-violent means, making violent acts incompatible with the movement's ideology.
 
• Any instance of violence during the movement led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement, as seen in the Chauri Chaura incident in 1922.
 
• The movement aimed to create mass non-violent resistance, including boycotts, strikes, and refusal to cooperate with British authorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refusal to pay taxes:**

 
 
• As part of the Non-Cooperation Movement, Indians were encouraged to refuse payment of taxes to the British government.
 
• This was a significant form of protest aimed at weakening the financial hold of the British administration over India.
 
• It symbolized the rejection of British authority and was a peaceful method of non-cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Boycott of British courts:**
 
 
• Gandhi urged lawyers and common citizens to boycott British courts and settle disputes through Indian arbitration systems.
 
• This was intended to delegitimize British legal institutions and promote self-reliance among Indians.
 
• The boycott of courts symbolized the refusal to accept British authority and reliance on indigenous systems.
 
 
 
• **Closure of schools and colleges:**
 
 
• Indian students were encouraged to leave government-run schools and colleges and join nationalist institutions such as Jamia Millia Islamia and Kashi Vidyapeeth.
 
• This was aimed at rejecting British education and promoting Indian values and culture.
 
• The closure of schools and colleges was a peaceful measure to oppose British rule and create self-sufficient educational systems.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement Theme:**
 
 
• The movement included boycotts of British goods, titles, and institutions, promoting indigenous alternatives (Swadeshi).
 
• It was rooted in non-violence and aimed to unite Indians across regional, religious, and caste lines against British rule.
 
• The movement marked a significant step toward India's independence struggle, emphasizing mass mobilization and peaceful resistance.

questions.question: The average weight of Rupesh, Mandar and Ketan is 45 kg. If the average weight of Rupesh and Mandar is 43 kg and that of Mandar and Ketan is 49 kg, then the weight of Mandar (in kg) is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total weight of **Rupesh, Mandar, and Ketan** = 45 × 3 = 135 kg.

Weight of **Mandar** = 184 − 135 = 49 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 49 kg.**

questions.question: The LCM of the numbers 4.7 and 0.04 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equate the number of **decimal places**: 4.70 and 0.04.

Remove decimals and find **LCM** of 470 and 4.

LCM(470, 4) = 940.

Place the decimal back at 2 places: 9.40.

**Given:** Numbers are **4.7** and **0.04**.

⇒ Required LCM = 940 ÷ 100 = 9.4.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.4.**

The HCF of a set of fractions is calculated as **HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators**.

questions.question: If 3 times Mary's present age is 22 years more than 5 times Dia's present age, and 3 times Dia's present age is 2 years less than Mary's present age, then what is the difference (in years) between the ages of Mary and Dia?

Let **Mary's age** be M and **Dia's age** be D.

From the second condition: M = 3D + 2

Substitute in the first condition: 3(3D + 2) = 5D + 22

⇒ 9D + 6 = 5D + 22 ⇒ 4D = 16 ⇒ D = 4

⇒ M = 3(4) + 2 = 14. Difference = 14 − 4 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Equation 2: 3 × **Dia's age** = **Mary's age** − 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ From Eq 2: M = 3D + 2

⇒ Substitute M in Eq 1: 3(3D + 2) = 5D + 22

⇒ 9D + 6 = 5D + 22

⇒ 9D − 5D = 22 − 6

⇒ 4D = 16

⇒ D = 4 years (**Dia's age**)

⇒ M = 3(4) + 2 = 14 years (**Mary's age**)

⇒ Difference = M − D = 14 − 4 = 10 years

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

questions.question: A man walks to a viewpoint and returns to the starting point by his car maintaining constant speed and thus takes a total time of 4 hours 30 minutes. He would have gained 2 hours by driving both ways. How long would it have taken for him to walk both ways with same walking speed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time gained or lost depends on the difference between **walking** and **driving** speeds.

Time saved by **driving both ways** instead of **walking/driving** = 2 hours.

This means **driving** saves 2 hours compared to **walking** for a one-way trip.

Total time for **walking both ways** = (Time for walk/drive) + (Time saved by driving) = 4 hr 30 min + 2 hr = 6 hr 30 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time for (**Walk + Drive**) = 4 hours 30 minutes = 4.5 hours

Time for (**Drive + Drive**) = 4 hours 30 minutes − 2 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes = 2.5 hours
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e17df3d101d535e14711b4790b8b6d8649d203c9791f147d6a9e5a96b4ee09de.png] 
Let **W** be the time taken to walk one way and **D** be the time taken to drive one way.

⇒ W + D = 4.5 hours --- (1)

⇒ 2D = 2.5 hours ⇒ D = 1.25 hours --- (2)

Substitute D in equation (1):

⇒ W + 1.25 = 4.5

⇒ W = 4.5 − 1.25 = 3.25 hours

Time to **walk both ways** = 2W

⇒ 2W = 2 × 3.25 = 6.5 hours

⇒ 6.5 hours = 6 hours 30 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time-Speed Inverse Relation

questions.question: The cost of 10 pens and 3 pencils is ₹129. If the cost of a pen decreases by ₹6 and the cost of a pencil increases by ₹9, then the cost of 8 pens and 2 pencils is ₹72. What is the original cost of 9 pens and 16 pencils?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **original cost** of a pen be **x** and a pencil be **y**.

New cost of 8 pens and 2 pencils = 8(x − 6) + 2(y + 9) = 72 ⇒ 8x + 2y = 72 + 48 − 18 = 102.

Solving 10x + 3y = 129 and 4x + y = 51 × 3 ⇒ 12x + 3y = 153.

Difference: 2x = 24 ⇒ **x = ₹12**; Substituting back: y = 51 − 48 = **₹3**.

Required: 9(12) + 16(3) = 108 + 48 = ₹156.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹156.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ 8P + 2p = 102 ⇒ 4P + p = 51 --- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Multiply Eq. 2 by 3: 12P + 3p = 153 --- (Eq. 3)

⇒ Subtract Eq. 1 from Eq. 3: (12P − 10P) = 153 − 129

⇒ 2P = 24 ⇒ **P = 12**

⇒ Put P = 12 in Eq. 2: 4(12) + p = 51 ⇒ 48 + p = 51 ⇒ **p = 3**

⇒ Cost of 9 pens and 16 pencils = 9 × 12 + 16 × 3

⇒ 108 + 48 = 156

**∴ The correct answer is ₹156.**
